title: Ellen's death
hookLine: his young wife Ellen died of tuberculosis after a short marriage

cards: Before the books, before strangers knew his name, there was Ellen. Ellen Tucker.
She was young, she wrote poems, and when Emerson married her she was already ill with tuberculosis, the coughing sickness people then called consumption. They had a short marriage. Then she died.
It's hard to understand the man who wrote about nature and the soul without knowing that he started out as a young widower.

teach.b: First, what they knew going in. Ellen's illness wasn't a surprise that arrived later. By the usual account, she was already sick during their engagement, and they married anyway.
They chose the time they had over the time they wanted.
Second, what his journal shows. After Ellen died, Emerson's entries return to her again and again. He doesn't write like a man who has neatly put grief away.
He writes like a man still talking to someone who isn't there.
And one entry, from some time after her death, records that he went to her tomb and opened the coffin. Readers have puzzled over that line. A man who couldn't yet believe she was gone?
Someone who needed to look death in the face before he could go on? The journal doesn't explain. It just says he did it.
Third, what came after. Within a short time he had left the pulpit, sailed to Europe, and begun the writing that made him known. Nobody can say exactly how much of that came from grief.
But the man who later wrote about finding the sacred in a field, in the stars, in an ordinary day, had already lost the person closest to him. Fourth, what early grief does.
A loss that comes young doesn't stay in the past.
It travels with you, sometimes quietly, into choices made years later.
Emerson didn't write a book about Ellen. Some readers hear her, all the same, behind the books he did write.

how: Biographers and readers of Emerson often turn to his journals from the years after Ellen Tucker Emerson's death to understand how early grief shaped his later writing about nature and the soul.

games.q: you're engaged to someone you love, and she is already seriously ill. what do you do?
o: wait to see whether she recovers.
marry her anyway, and take the time you have.
games.why: by the usual account, Emerson and Ellen married anyway, knowing she was ill. they had a short marriage before she died.

practice: Let your mind go back to an early loss, a person, a pet, a place, a friendship that ended, a version of yourself; if a heavy one comes and it's too much right now, choose a smaller one, or simply breathe.
You don't need to relive it, just notice that it's still with you, and where it went in your life afterward.
If grief ever feels like more than you can carry, or you think about harming yourself, call or text 988 in the US, or your local emergency number.
